system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Project Kestrel — Buyer review of Seller positions

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Wattlebridge should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. Seller says the positions are final, but that is not buyer approval. | **25% / AUD 6m** cap. The 20% fallback is available only with prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The proposed fallback is not authorised under the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis and **AUD 250,000** tipping basket, with recovery only above the basket. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis and **AUD 50,000** aggregate tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook levels.** Seller’s thresholds materially narrow recovery and its basket improperly excludes the first dollars. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | **18 months** after Completion; Seller also proposes applying any claim limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | General Warranty Claims period of **24 months** after Completion; no blanket extension of general limitations to other claim categories. The 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject; counter at 24 months and preserve separate regimes.** Neither the shorter period nor its proposed spillover is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; draft the separate regime.** Title and capacity exposure should not be diluted by general-warranty limits. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; add the carve-out.** The playbook does not permit waiver of these protections. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific disclosures are also included. | Specific, fair disclosure; reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable through a prudent search. | **Reject the blanket disclosure language; retain only specific fair disclosure.** General access to records does not identify the matters being disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion. If a knowledge qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete or tightly qualify it.** Constructive or adviser knowledge could otherwise defeat claims without a fair disclosure standard. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of condition satisfaction are absent. | Effective Bluefen consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. | **Reject; make both items a Completion condition.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and delivery alone does not establish compliance with consent conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms no repayment or final security discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release as drafted; require the specified payoff and release mechanics.** The facility and security remain outstanding on the disclosed facts. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** DD-005 bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding for the bonuses and triggered on-costs; no silent exclusion. | **Reject the current funds flow; quantify and expressly allocate bonuses and on-costs.** The disclosure confirms the bonuses are absent from the draft funds flow. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 makes transfer conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010’s **AUD 180,000** open amount is not independently verified, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. | Broaden the indemnity to cover the relevant Ironquay IP/title and transfer risks while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not assume the AUD 180,000 is either verified as due or paid. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve a documented cure.** The materials show a transfer condition and an unresolved payment/assignment position. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material. Disclosure says access, scope and notification obligations are unestablished; no loss amount is stated. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; do not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Do not accept a materiality conclusion or assert an established breach; require preservation and ongoing reporting.** The disclosed investigation remains preliminary and key facts are unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total **AUD 330,000** and are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess timing, scope and contractual status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure leaves the relevant liability and termination facts unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says Tax and IP are settled under the general regime; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims in their appropriate separate categories, with no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket override; state the regimes and interactions expressly.** A general-claims clause should not silently determine distinct claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on the DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; treat DD-012 as a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification and supporting evidence.** The register identifies the source relied upon but does not independently verify title or encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms open for negotiation; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **Do not treat them as agreed; continue negotiating expressly.** The playbook records these terms as open, with no approved resolution. |
=== END ADVICE ===
